sets.name: Research
sets.covers: Interviews, surveys, usability tests, diary studies, card sorts, affinity diagrams, empathy maps, personas, journey maps, jobs to be done and research repositories.
sets.why: Left alone, Claude will write you a persona from nothing. This set gives it a method for asking real people first.
sets.missing: So far these have only run on made-up test data, and none has been compared with no skill at all.

intro: Everything here is typed by name, and every name starts with `/ux-os:`. Not sure where to start? `/ux-os:research-next` says where an idea stands and the one thing to do now.

Personas, journeys, jobs and empathy maps each take a switch. `proto` builds from what you believe and labels it an assumption. `real` builds from your files, and every line links to the exact passage it came from. Real needs at least 5 people from different organisations, and stops if you don't have them.
Run `/ux-os:init` once per project and deliverables take your design system's fonts and colours. Design proposals then name a real component, or say none fits.
runIt.promptsNote: Swap volunteer-rota for your own idea, in two to four words.
prompts: I have an idea and no data yet.
I want a quick persona from what I already believe.
I've finished my interviews and want real personas.
I've talked to five organisations and want to stop guessing.
I don't know what to do next.
I want deliverables to look like our design system.
runIt.installIntro: Install it once. You need Claude Code, and Node for the checking scripts.

sets.name: Design systems
sets.covers: Tokens, components, naming, governance and documentation.
sets.why: Claude reaches for whatever value looks right. These hold it to the tokens and components you already chose.
sets.missing: ds-kit builds and changes a system now, from foundations to release, but it has never run on a real public website.

sets.name: Information architecture
sets.covers: Content inventories, card sorts, taxonomies, labels, sitemaps, navigation, URL rules, content models, redirects, tree tests and findability.
sets.why: Where things go decides whether anyone finds them. It's also the one set with a skill tested end to end.
sets.missing: Nothing outstanding. In one run of the same three test cases, the split scored 28 of 29 and the single skill 25 of 29.

sets.name: Interaction design
sets.covers: States, forms, feedback, errors, navigation patterns, UX laws and motion.
sets.why: The happy path is the easy part. This set covers what happens on an error, during a load and when someone changes their mind.
sets.missing: Blind judges split my eleven against MC Dean's pack three and three, and preferred plain Claude on the three longest jobs, because mine run long. So MC Dean's pack leads and mine run by name.

sets.name: Visual design
sets.covers: Hierarchy, colour, type, layout, visual critique and page craft.
sets.why: Hierarchy and type are where AI-made pages start to look alike. These give Claude a way to see that and correct it.

sets.name: Content
sets.covers: UX writing, voice and tone, microcopy, editing and content strategy.
sets.why: Words are most of the interface. Claude writes fluent copy by default, which isn't the same as copy in your voice.
sets.missing: Nothing of mine for UX writing or voice yet. The VOICE.md project file is the first piece.

sets.name: Prototyping
sets.covers: Wireframes, user flows, concept selection, prototype strategy, test plans and heuristic evaluation.
sets.why: A prototype exists to kill an idea cheaply. This set decides what to build, how rough it can be and what counts as a pass.
sets.missing: Design OS links the object map, sitemap, flows, screens, wireframes and a lo-fi prototype into checked files. It has passed on one worked example, not on a real project.

sets.name: UX strategy
sets.covers: Problem framing, briefs, vision, opportunities and metrics.
sets.why: A fast answer to the wrong problem is still wrong. This set makes Claude frame the problem before it touches a screen.
sets.missing: After a fix that puts the finished deliverable first, blind judges split mine and plain Claude five and five, up from two of ten. Not yet tested on new cases.

sets.name: AI-XD
sets.covers: AI experience design: conversation, trust, guardrails and agent handoffs.
sets.why: Designing for a model is its own discipline. Trust, refusal, handoff and recovery all need designing on purpose.
sets.missing: Three more packs are installed and switched off.

sets.name: Orchestration
sets.covers: Running the other sets against a real target until it meets a bar.
sets.why: The other sets are methods. This one runs them against a real page and keeps going until it holds up.

sets.name: Accessibility and inclusion
sets.covers: Inclusive personas, cognitive access, accessible content and adaptive interfaces.
sets.why: Access decided at the end gets cut. This set starts with who's being left out.
sets.missing: Five of the six packs are switched off.

sets.name: Design ops and communication
sets.covers: Handoff, critique process, sprints, rationale and case studies.
sets.why: Good design still has to survive the handoff and the meeting. This set covers what happens around the file.
sets.missing: Eleven program and leadership packs are switched off.

entries.name: claims-auditor
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Checks a /ux-os:run work file: whether its claims table is complete and whether each citation supports its claim. Writes one audit file and edits nothing else.

entries.name: researcher
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: General research agent for interviews, usability tests, surveys, personas, journeys and synthesis, plus best-practice research. Consolidated from several role agents.

entries.name: init
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Connects a project's design system once. Deliverables take its fonts and colours, and each design proposal names a real component or says none fits. It shows you everything before saving.
entries.proof: Connected to one real design system with 133 components. The step that saves it has its own self-test, and running it twice changes nothing.

entries.name: record-decision
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Records what you decided because of the research, what the decision rests on and what would reverse it. A decision made on a belief stays in pencil.
entries.proof: The rules its file is checked against have their own self-test and one independent review. The typed command has not been run yet.

entries.name: research-debrief
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Takes in a new interview or study, removes the names, and shows which beliefs it bears on, without rewriting anything you built.
entries.proof: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.

entries.name: research-discover
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Asks what you believe about a new idea, once, then builds your first jobs, personas and journey from it and names the one belief to test first.
entries.proof: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.
entries.credit: Chaining models into one command comes from MC Dean's discover command in the Designer Skills Pack.

entries.name: research-next
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Says where a research idea stands and the one thing to run next. It reads the folder and changes nothing.
entries.proof: Typed as a real command on a made-up idea, and it named the right next step. The routing has its own self-test.
entries.credit: The one-command-now shape comes from MC Dean's start-here command in the Designer Skills Pack.

entries.name: research-synthesize
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Once enough evidence is in, sorts it, summarises it, settles each belief and rebuilds your proto models on what people did.
entries.proof: Run by an agent following the files, on made-up test data only.
entries.credit: Chaining synthesis into one command comes from MC Dean's synthesize command in the Designer Skills Pack.

entries.name: run
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Runs someone else's design skill on an idea without changing it, then files the output with a table of every claim it rests on, each tagged. A separate auditor reads the table.
entries.proof: The briefing and the check have their own self-tests. Followed by agents on two walk-throughs. The typed command has not been run yet, and picks cover six interaction design jobs only.

entries.name: affinity-diagram
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Sorts real research notes into themes from the bottom up, counts people rather than notes, and has a second agent re-sort them blind. Needs data to work from.
entries.proof: Test run: 4 of 26 notes landed differently in the blind re-sort. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: analyze-card-sort
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Works out how people grouped your cards: how often pairs stayed together, the groups that form, and the cards with no clear home. Needs real results.
entries.proof: Analysis script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-diary-study
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A diary study people will finish: entries under two minutes, a plan for dropouts, and everything participants receive.
prompts: /ux-os:create-diary-study how often shifts fall through over a month
entries.proof: Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-empathy-map
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Maps what one person says, does, thinks and feels in one moment, and where saying and doing come apart. Works from your beliefs or from real research.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-interview-script
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A short guide built on real past events, with every question tied to something it tests, read cold by a second agent before anyone runs it.
prompts: /ux-os:create-interview-script why coordinators stop using shared calendars
entries.proof: Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-journey-map
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Maps what happens today, or what should happen in future, from your beliefs or from real research. A future journey is labelled as a proposal.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-jtbd
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Works out what people are trying to get done, apart from any product, from your beliefs or from the stories of people who actually switched.
entries.proof: A false belief planted in the test came back contradicted. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-personas
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Splits people on the behaviour that most changes what they need. Works from your beliefs, each one marked and tested, or from real research.
entries.proof: Checking script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-research-repository
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: One place for what you've learned across studies, with each insight's strength and age, that answers questions without guessing.
prompts: /ux-os:create-research-repository ask what do we know about no-shows
entries.proof: Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-service-blueprint
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Lays out how a service delivers one scenario, step by step, with what the person sees above the line and what makes it work below.
prompts: /ux-os:create-service-blueprint volunteer-rota a coordinator fills one open shift
entries.proof: The rules its file is checked against have their own self-test and one independent review. Filled once from an existing blueprint. The typed command has not been run yet.

entries.name: create-survey
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Writes the analysis first, then only the questions it needs, with sample sizes worked out by a script.
prompts: /ux-os:create-survey how many coordinators still run the rota on paper
entries.proof: Sample size script with its own self-test. Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: create-usability-plan
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Realistic tasks and pass lines set before anyone is tested, so the result can't be argued into a pass.
entries.proof: Run on made-up test data only.

entries.name: summarize-research
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Turns a transcript or a study into findings rated by how many people stand behind them, with what cuts against each. Needs real data.
entries.proof: Its draft passed the checks, but it hasn't yet written its output file in a test.

entries.name: design-research
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Personas, empathy maps, journey maps, interview scripts, surveys, diary studies, card sort analysis, usability test plans and synthesis. Switched back on 13 November 2026.

entries.name: lenny-skills research set
entries.author: RefoundAI
entries.summary: customer-interviews and analyzing-user-feedback, from a much larger skills library.

entries.name: design-system agent
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Drives live page violations to zero without changing how a page looks unless a person approves it.

entries.name: workshopr-uxdrift
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Audits a codebase for UX drift against its DESIGN.md and design-system JSON, and keeps the report to about fifteen findings so it gets read.

entries.name: Design System Enforcer
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Checks UI code against a design system's tokens and components.
entries.installNote: Clone the repo and add it as an MCP server. The README has the steps.
entries.proof: Ships with its own test suite.

entries.name: adopt-ds
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Moves an existing page or app onto the system, replacing hardcoded colours and one-off styles.

entries.name: connect-ds
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Connects a repo that already has a design system, writing the profile the other ds-kit skills read.

entries.name: create-components
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Builds a first set of components from an inventory on shared conventions, with a machine-readable catalog and a real keyboard pass.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 7 of 7 outcome checks with the skill, 6 of 7 without (12 of 12 with its own checks). 606s and $1.12 with, 40s and $0.14 without, the most expensive skill in the set. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-design-system
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Starts a design system from a live website, telling what a team meant from what drifted, and asks a person to rule on what the numbers cannot settle. Also takes a moodboard pick.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 9 of 9 outcome checks with the skill, 8 of 9 without (20 of 20 with its own checks). 88s and $0.27 with, 38s and $0.17 without. A second case confirms it stops and asks when someone is there to answer. Trigger test 3 of 3.

entries.name: create-design-tokens
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Builds a tiered token layer in DTCG 2025.10, or rebuilds a flat pile in a live codebase without breaking what reads it.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 8 of 9 outcome checks with the skill, 7 of 9 without (13 of 14 with its own checks). 151s and $0.37 with, 45s and $0.14 without. The one miss: a notice kept the same red in dark mode. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-ds-site
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Generates a documentation site from the system's own files so it cannot disagree with them, and fails when it goes stale.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 6 of 6 outcome checks with the skill, 5 of 6 without (11 of 11 with its own checks). 283s and $0.19 with, 87s and $0.28 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-foundations
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Decides colour, type, space, grid, elevation and motion from the product's real conditions, with every number marked as observed, chosen, derived or assumed.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 5 of 8 without (13 of 13 with its own checks). 58s and $0.17 with, 84s and $0.22 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-icon-system
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Decides whether to adopt, curate or draw an icon set, then delivers a checked sprite, manifest and wrapper without quietly redrawing anything.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 8 of 8 without (15 of 15 with its own checks). 57s and $0.23 with, 53s and $0.16 without. No gain on outcomes alone; the gain is the contract and what it refuses to do. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-moodboard
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Chooses a visual direction before any tokens exist: two or three directions to pick between, written down as a brief.

entries.name: create-patterns
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Documents recurring compositions from real screens, and turns away what is only a page or a single component.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 4 of 5 outcome checks with the skill, 1 of 5 without (10 of 11 with its own checks). 200s and $0.50 with, 42s and $0.18 without. The no-skill score swung from 5 of 5 to 1 of 5 between rounds, so read it as noisy. The one miss was a phrase the check did not recognise: the run did reject the hero. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: ds-governance
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Sets ownership and rules sized to the team, each rule either enforced by a gate or a named reviewer, or labelled a convention.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 8 of 8 outcome checks with the skill, 4 of 8 without (13 of 13 with its own checks). 71s and $0.23 with, 33s and $0.11 without. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.name: migrate-ds
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Renames, deprecates, merges or removes a token or component, with a codemod rather than find and replace.

entries.name: release-ds
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Cuts a design-system version: decides the version number and writes the changelog.

entries.name: sync-ds-figma
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Pushes tokens to Figma variables and settles which side is right when Figma and code disagree.

entries.name: update-design-system
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: One change that spans tokens, components and names together, such as a rebrand or adding dark mode.

entries.name: update-ds-components
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Adds a component or changes an existing one's options, markup or API.

entries.name: update-ds-tokens
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Adds a design token or changes a value safely, including the one-line tweaks that look trivial.

entries.name: validate-ai-readability
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Measures whether a fresh AI agent can use a design system, by counting what it invents across blind builds.
entries.proof: Final run, one case: 7 of 7 outcome checks with the skill, 6 of 7 without (12 of 13 with its own checks). 110s and $0.71 with, 32s and $0.16 without. The one miss: that run did not render its builds, and said so. Trigger test 2 of 2.

entries.summary: Copy strategy and look before any code, a hero-first build, gates against generic AI pages and a two-reviewer feedback round.

entries.name: create-content-strategy
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: What to publish, what to stop and who keeps the rest alive, sized to the team's real capacity.
entries.proof: Script with 105 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 10, old 10. Blind judge: new first, old second, no skill third. Round 1: no skill first, new last. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

entries.name: prototyping-testing
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Wireframe specs, user flows, parallel concepts, concept selection, prototype strategy, test scenarios, click tests, heuristic evaluation, accessibility test plans and A/B tests.

entries.name: prototype
entries.author: Matt Pocock
entries.summary: Builds a quick prototype to test an idea.

entries.name: user-flow-diagram
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Diagrams screen-level paths, decision points and branch logic for how a feature is traversed.

entries.name: align-stakeholders
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Works out what kind of disagreement it is, separates what was said from what is inferred, and gets a decision recorded.
entries.proof: Script with 124 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 10. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: analyze-competitors
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A competitive read that changes a decision, with every claim sourced and dated and a check on whether weights flip the ranking.
entries.proof: Script with 65 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: business-design
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Whether an idea can make money: the bet that would kill it, unit economics, pricing and the cheapest test.
entries.proof: Script with 79 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 9, old 8. Blind judge: new first, no skill second, old third. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-brief
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: One page that turns a request into an agreement about the problem, with contradictions and open questions first.
entries.proof: Script with 107 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 10. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

entries.name: create-design-principles
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Principles that settle arguments, ranked for when they collide and tested on disputes set aside first.
entries.proof: Script with 80 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second. Round 1: new first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-experience-map
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Where an experience breaks across channels and owners, with every cell marked evidence or assumption.
entries.proof: Script with 92 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 9 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 1 of 2.

entries.name: create-manifesto
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A manifesto of positions that cost something, each tested against a real decision, with receipts.
entries.proof: Script with 75 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: no skill first, new second, same as round 1. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-north-star
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A vision or a single metric, how it could be gamed, its guardrails and what a target really demands.
entries.proof: Script with 171 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 10 of 10, no skill 9. Blind judge: new first, no skill second. Round 1: no skill first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: create-service-blueprint
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: What has to be true backstage for a promise to hold: lanes, owners, failures and recoveries, with times computed.
entries.proof: Script with 68 self-tests. Sealed case, round 2 after the deliverable-first fix, 9 Nov 2026: 8 of 10, no skill 10, old 10. Blind judge: no skill first, old second, new third. Round 1: new first. Trigger check: 2 of 2.

entries.name: design-ops
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Handoff specs, critique and review process, design QA, sprints, design debt and impact reporting.

entries.name: designer-toolkit
entries.author: MC Dean
entries.summary: Design rationale, case studies, presentations, UX writing, negotiation and design-system adoption.

entries.name: Design Agent
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: A self-looping designer: critique, fix, re-render and re-score until an exit bar is met, then learn from the run.
entries.proof: An independent critic scores every pass.

entries.name: critique-partner
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Design critic that judges a page against the project's written rules. Every issue quotes a rule word for word and points at evidence on the page; anything no rule covers is labelled a judgment call.

entries.name: design-critic
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Independent scorer for each Design Agent pass. Looks at the rendered page and the code with fresh eyes, scores them against the contract and never fixes anything.

entries.name: feature-build
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Builds one slice of a planned feature and loops it until lint, tests, the design system and review all pass.
entries.proof: An independent reviewer scores every pass.

entries.name: feature-plan
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Interviews you into a spec, a design brief and build slices, then runs the feature pipeline.
entries.proof: Its test suites were all green on 20 Oct 2026.

entries.name: crit
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Interactive critique of a URL, page, screenshot or Figma frame against the project's own taste.md and design rules. It captures the page, asks what the page is for one question at a time, then runs the critique-partner agent.
entries.proof: A gate with 55 test cases, and two headless runs.

entries.name: create-project-files
entries.author: Bill Bulman and Claude
entries.summary: Sets up a project's nine UX-OS files (PRODUCT, DESIGN, AGENTS, PERSONAS, JOURNEYS, JTBD, taste, motion and VOICE) from annotated templates, writing only the ones that are missing.
